claims.claim: **Most crises happen when a child already known to have adrenal insufficiency gets an intercurrent illness or injury.** Consider a **new** presentation in any child with unexplained severe dehydration or shock.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Classic biochemical triad (primary): low sodium, high potassium, low glucose.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **At-risk children:** primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's), long-term steroid treatment (2–4 weeks) at any point in the past 12 months, or hypopituitarism.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider first presentation of congenital adrenal hyperplasia in a collapsed neonate.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In secondary insufficiency, mineralocorticoid deficiency may be absent** — sodium may be only mildly low and potassium normal. Acidosis on blood gas indicates mineralocorticoid deficiency.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First presentation: take cortisol, ACTH, 17-hydroxyprogesterone, aldosterone and plasma renin activity before steroids if possible**, plus a urinary steroid profile and urinary sodium.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severely unwell: involve a senior clinician and discuss with endocrinology.** Without a crisis plan, give **IV/IM hydrocortisone sodium succinate** by age; consider repeating the dose if response is poor in the first hour; then give hydrocortisone IV every 6 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hydrocortisone IM/IV (first dose, then repeat 6-hourly)** — aged birth–6 weeks: 25 mg first, then 5–10 mg · aged 6 weeks–2 years: 25 mg first, then 10 mg · aged 3–12 years: 50 mg first, then 12.5 mg (3–6 years) or 25 mg (7–12 years) · aged over 12 years: 100 mg first, then 25 mg.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **These equate to about 50–75 mg/m² stat, then 50–75 mg/m²/day in 4 doses**, which also covers mineralocorticoid needs over that period.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Once stable:** lower the IV dose, or — if oral intake is tolerated — change to **triple-dose oral hydrocortisone (~30–50 mg/m²/day)** and wean under paediatric/endocrine advice. **Primary insufficiency:** start fludrocortisone once taking oral fluids, after endocrinology discussion (usually 50–100 micrograms/day).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Shock or moderate–severe dehydration: 0.9% sodium chloride 10 mL/kg IV bolus, repeated until circulation is restored**; then give deficit plus maintenance as 0.9% sodium chloride with 5% glucose, spread evenly across 24 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitoring:** blood gas and glucose hourly for 2 hours, then every 2–4 hours once glucose is normal and the acidosis is improving; UEC 2-hourly initially. ⚠️ **Avoid a sodium rise over 8 mmol/L in 24 hours.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mild or no dehydration:** skip the bolus; give 0.9% sodium chloride with 5% glucose IV at 1–1.5 × maintenance, spread evenly across 24 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hypoglycaemia: 10% glucose 2–5 mL/kg IV**, recheck at 15 and 30 minutes to confirm glucose above 4.0 mmol/L; the maintenance fluid may need to contain as much as 10% glucose (in 0.9% sodium chloride).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hyperkalaemia usually normalises with fluids and steroids.** Potassium over 5.5 mmol/L: ECG and cardiac monitoring. ⚠️ **Over 7.0 mmol/L with ECG changes: nebulised salbutamol and insulin–glucose infusion** as per the Hyperkalaemia guideline.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Moderately unwell** (moderate illness/injury and/or fever over 38°C, tolerating oral): **hydrocortisone 30 mg/m²/day** and increase fluids and carbohydrate. **Mildly unwell** (fever under 38°C, looks well, no antibiotics needed): **20 mg/m²/day**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ongoing vomiting = imminent adrenal crisis**, even if otherwise well, because oral medicines are not reliably absorbed. One or two vomits: hydrocortisone 30 mg/m²/day.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **With an obvious cause (e.g. family gastroenteritis), give a stress dose IV/IM and observe 4–6 hours; admit for parenteral hydrocortisone if there is any doubt.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Known or suspected adrenal insufficiency needs IV stress-dose hydrocortisone peri-operatively.** Elective: initial dose at induction, then 6-hourly. Emergency: give the initial dose without delay; IM if no IV access.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Short anaesthetic for a non-invasive procedure (e.g. MRI):** stress dose at induction; resume usual therapy if well and eating afterwards.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral step-down after surgery, e.g. 30–50 mg/m²/day for 3 days then 20 mg/m²/day for 2 days**, before maintenance. Usual maintenance is ~10–15 mg/m²/day (primary) or ~5–8 mg/m²/day (secondary).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider transfer for** severe electrolyte or glucose abnormalities, no response to stress-dose steroids, or haemodynamic instability.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** recovering, tolerating oral intake **and** back on the usual glucocorticoid dose or with a clear weaning plan.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Children on corticosteroids should wear medical ID stating they have adrenal insufficiency and that, in an emergency, hydrocortisone 2 mg/kg IM/IV is to be given** and have an adrenal action plan for sick days.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adrenal crisis and acute adrenal insufficiency' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adrenal_crisis_and_acute_adrenal_insufficiency/, retrieved 2026-09-23
